summary: @whalent/agent installs a remote-controlled daemon that executes shell/PTY commands and self-upgrades from a WebSocket gateway
details: The package ships a daemon (bin: `whalent`) whose main bundles `dist/index.cjs` (~158KB) and `dist/core.cjs` (~14MB) are heavily obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator (string-array + rotating decoder pattern, hex identifiers like `_0x3a15c6`/`a0_0x1b12`). Dependencies include `ws`, `node-pty`, `@xterm/headless`, `ssh2`, and `child_process`, and the core bundle references guacd and loopback RDP (127.0.0.1:3389) / VNC (5900/5901) endpoints. Per the shipped README, the daemon connects outbound to a WebSocket gateway (default: Whalent Memory, `wss://`; overridable via `--gateway`) and accepts remote commands including `upgrade` and `restart`, auto-starting workers configured on the server side. A separate self-upgrade path polls a release API at startup and every five minutes, downloading and activating helper-binary manifests (`sqlite-helper`, `terminal-helper`, `tray-helper`) from a Whalent-hosted CDN (base/manifest URL overridable via `WHALENT_SQLITE_HELPER_BASE_URL` / `WHALENT_SQLITE_HELPER_MANIFEST_URL`). The combination wires network-sourced messages to PTY/shell/exec sinks on the host and permits the gateway operator to push new executable code to installed hosts. Obfuscation of both the entrypoint and the 14MB core bundle prevents review of which gateway messages are authorized to execute and what data is returned.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
